newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: CRH says full-year outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: CRH says full-year outlook positive.

text.p: Irish-based building materials group CRH Plc said on Wednesday the outlook for its full-year performance was positive with growth in the U.S. and Ireland continuing to drive profits forward.

"The outlook for the remainder of the year is generally positive with Ireland and North America continuing to perform strongly," chief executive Don Godson said in CRH's half-year results statement. "Overall, we anticipate a further year of progress for the group," he said.
CRH reported a 13 percent increase in half-year pre-tax profits to 64.1 million Irish pounds.
CRH also announced the acquisition of BTR's U.S. unit Tilcon for $329 million, and the placement of 17.94 million shares to raise 101 million punts.
The company said first-half growth had been driven by the Irish and U.S. markets.
"Increases in underlying profits in Ireland and the U.S. together with contributions from recent acquisitions were partly offset by declines in the UK and mainland Europe," Godson said.
CRH said construction activity remained buoyant in Ireland with strong demand from all sectors although a moderation in growth levels and decline in agricultural investment was likely.
"North America, as always, constitutes a number of regional economies, many of which are performing strongly but some of which are still weak," CRH said.
"Our operations are benefiting from the general health of the U.S. economy and recent acquisitions are performing to expectations," it said.
But the outlook for Britain and mainland Europe was less good, the company said.
"Markets in Britain remain difficult with little evidence to date from our operations of the forecast upturn in demand," it said.
It said that although its businesses in the Benelux countries were recovering, full-year profits in Spain were not expected to match its 1995 levels.

CRH said strategic acquisitions and new investments would also underpin its progress this year. Its policy of actively seeking bolt-on acquisitions would continue unabated despite the purchase of Tilcon, it said.
Bad weather affected first-half profits in the Benelux countries, North America and Britain, although profits in North America increased despite the weather, CRH said.
